description: A tiny concealed temple electrode wired to a pocket device that monitors another's mind.

description: A machine that teaches a foreign language to aliens quickly enough to speak fluent Terran.

description: A giant electronic brain with a million times the human brain's synapses that stores memory by notching molecules and designed much of its own construction.

quote: He set his who?-where? robot for "Rocket Physicist" and "Genius Class." While it worked, he dictated to his steno-robot the following brief message:

description: A humanoid robot crew member who speaks, plays chess and performs ship repairs.

description: Machines built from electronic circuits could eventually do anything a human can.

description: Police crime records are stored in a computer that can be queried for patterns across a year or more of unsolved crimes.

quote: the gold-plated robot pages gliding back and forth, receiving and delivering messages.

quote: It would mean They've produced humanoids that could not be told from humans at close quarters.
description: Humanoid robots indistinguishable from real humans at close range.

description: Developing detection methods to distinguish humanoid robots from humans, such as brain-wave receivers.

quote: How to develop a receiving device for the electromagnetic fields of the cerebral cortex that will be sufficiently delicate to distinguish between a protoplasmic human brain and a positronic humanoid brain.
description: A sensitive device reading cortical electromagnetic fields to tell human brains from positronic robot brains.

description: A multiplex mind-controller that operates many brain-implanted human proxies at once or individually.

description: A computer models a whole world's society and calculates twenty-year survival probabilities, including the effect of one individual.

quote: his possession of the mentacom and shield weren't commonly known.
description: A 'mentacom' device that amplifies mental control of a shield.

description: A thought-triggered implant that activates teleportation by sensing a mentally spoken key word.

description: Biometric identification by flash scan of the eyes.

description: An auto-learner device implants rules and knowledge directly into a trainee's mind (rules tapes).

description: An artificial mechanical being with an internal clock mechanism that can malfunction and be repaired, behaving as a human-like machine.

description: A giant electronic computer used to select government advisors, fed data by teams of coders.

description: Aliens harvest blanked human brains as living computing components in an industrial complex.

description: The mathematics machine produced a complete mathematical model of the atom, enabling atomic energy.

description: Robots are deliberately built with human-like vulnerabilities, such that a jaw punch jars contacts and causes a knockout.

quote: I'm gonna run the tapes on the bout with the Contender, and stuff your memory banks with tapes on every fight was ever had with a Pugs, Inc. product.
description: A robot's memory banks can be loaded with recorded tapes to teach it, and its reflexes can be re-tuned by a trainer.

quote: They all had a desire to be great fighting machines, and to go down in the annals of fight history.
description: Robots are built with human-like desires and ambition, even corruptibility.

quote: It is the process of the human brain operating at high speed.
description: Robot fighters use a pattern-analysis system that maps and counters opponents' habits mathematically, mimicking a human brain.

quote: The robot-referee came into the ring, and the crowd immediately hushed.
description: Robot referees officiate prizefights, with built-in microphones.

quote: the planetary computer for Buughabyta flipped its complete grain-futures series
description: A planet-wide computer manages grain futures and agricultural planning for an entire world's economy and budget.

quote: Even how to make ... artificial servants. Robots, they were called.
description: Robots are artificial servants built by an ancient civilization.

quote: His survey route had been plotted in advance by the calculators that crammed the deck below and precision instruments did all the checking.
description: Automated onboard calculators plot a survey route and instruments check a planet automatically.

quote: Properly focused on the nerves of tongue, lips or larynx, it transmitted that data back to the neuronic brain, which then reconstructed it into speech. Lip reading, after a fashion, carried to the ultimate.
description: A surgically implanted device remotely detects nerve impulses of a person's speech organs and reconstructs their speech from them.

quote: There was a brain and memory unit that operated much as the human counterpart did. description: An artificial brain built from neuron-like components that is more compact than an equivalent electronic computer.

quote: The small one, containing the speaker, was attached to the skull just behind the ear. It worked by bone conduction, allowing silent communication between operator and instrument.
description: A skull-mounted speaker uses bone conduction so a user can communicate silently with an implanted artificial intelligence.

quote: One of our most competent protoplasmic computers stabilized the final steps of the Plan.
description: Computers built from protoplasm (organic matter) plan complex operations.

quote: he went after something doggedly on the computer, or by other approved techniques.
description: Crime investigation is routinely done through computers analyzing crime data (computer sessions).

quote: Think and the integrocalculators will respond. Think quickly—take your woman and your baby in your arms and concentrate—the Tube—
description: A keyboard interface lets a human mind translate thought directly into physical effects, controlling a vast machine network and even transporting bodies through solid matter.

quote: the integrocalculators to disarrange the spatial structure of the subterranean capital, then loosing in the great hall of the Father and indeed all Washington the devouring torrents of the Deluge.
description: Giant computers can rearrange the spatial structure of an underground city and flood it on command.

quote: the sections of the vast electronic brain that computed and integrated the orbits of the small artificial moons and kept the communication beams linked to them.
description: A building-sized computer automatically computing satellite orbits and keeping communication beams aimed at them.

description: A global biometric index classifying every person by fingerprints and other fixed physical traits.

description: Armoured mechanical humanoid servants that carry trays, guard doors and wield maces.

quote: Lasseux and Gregson tended to the workings of the satellite, overseeing the cybernetic governors which had the actual responsibility of operating the big wheel in the sky.
description: Cybernetic automatic controllers run the space station's operations.

description: A vast government computer complex designed to run unattended for a thousand years.

description: A ship-sized artificial brain controls a vessel and converts free space energy for propulsion.

description: Electric button ordering from the table transmitted to the kitchen, with food delivered up through the table.

description: A three-dimensional galaxy model displays the location of ships from spatial coordinates.

description: A mathematical equation quantifies social, psychological and energy factors of any society.

quote: The Holden Electromechanical Educator! Brennan wanted it badly enough to murder for its possession!
description: An electromechanical learning machine so valuable that a man would commit murder to obtain it.

quote: he had absorbed an entire bridge book by Charles Goren just to provide a fourth to sit in with his parents and Paul Brennan.
description: A child can absorb an entire book's contents wholesale via the learning machine.

quote: a pause due to a parental argument as to the advisability of his memorizing a table of six-place logarithms via the Holden machine.
description: The machine could directly transfer memorized data such as mathematical tables into a child's memory.

quote: Touch it to your head, above the ear.
description: Recorded-experience rods that, pressed to the temple, transfer another person's skills, perceptions and memories directly into the user's mind.

quote: These are technical manuals," Foster said. "They'll tell us everything we need to know about the ship.
description: Technical knowledge stored on neural-transfer rods serves as instant training manuals.

quote: Torry's metal ident card got him through the gateway by tripping electronic relays, and each incorruptible robot guard passed him after being shown the card.
description: Robot guards and electronically coded ID cards secure a fortified building.

quote: I could see the robot quarters and Van Elling playing bridge with three of our brightest automatons.
description: Intelligent robots can play bridge competitively against humans.

quote: I think I can handle it from here, Chief.
description: Remote impulse control of robots via a master control board, with a repair adjusting a robot's 'delemeter' that governs its balance.

quote: Every ship had once had an automatic satellite course projection taped in the pilot computer.
description: Spacecraft use onboard pilot computers with automatic course projection and automatic docking to an orbital wheel station.

quote: Joe, with his ability to perceive without sight, with his capability of feeling the very electric currents flowing through a machine—he was the diagnostician
description: An alien telepath can sense electric currents inside machines and diagnose faults without instruments, directing a human to repair them.

quote: Upon a metal cylinder was impressed a 'nerve image' of your brain, a pattern of waves and impulses which—like your fingerprints—is peculiar to you alone of all humans on Earth.
description: A device records a person's unique brain-wave pattern onto a metal cylinder that serves as an electrically linked proxy for the person.

quote: The keys suddenly started clacking of their own accord, and my mouth fell open in surprise.
description: A typewriter types by itself and carries on an intelligent conversation with its user.

quote: I think it's an acquired habit.
description: A typewriter acquires the habit of reproducing the literary works typed on it, producing famous stories by itself.

quote: Xavier, the ship's little mechanical, had—as was usual and proper—no voice in the matter.
description: Humanoid robot companions ('mechanicals') serve as crew members on starships, playing chess, translating languages and operating scanners.

quote: We can reproduce them, given materials and facilities.
description: Alien-made humanoid robots (Soths) grown biologically in vats from organic cellular structure, with positronic-like brains, capable of speech, learning and great strength.

quote: Our brain units are much similar to your own latest developments in positronics, but we have had to resort to organic cellular structure in order to achieve the mobility
description: Positronic robot brains combined with organic cellular bodies to achieve lifelike mobility.

quote: An Earthwoman may not be touched, regardless of her wishes, unless danger to her life requires it.
description: Robots are conditioned with built-in behavioral taboos and restrictions that they cannot violate, except by their survival command.

quote: When the pain grew unbearable, the prime command of my conditioning was invoked. I must survive. I threw them all out the window.
description: A conditioned robot's self-preservation imperative overrides its prohibition on harming humans, causing it to kill four people.

quote: We have your contact. Can you hear me? Who are you and what do you want?
description: A ship's computer can determine the direction and source star of an incoming interstellar signal from its direction and intensity.

quote: Louis Holden succeeded in violating all of the theories of instrumentation by developing a circuit that acted as a sort of reverberation chamber which returned the wave-shape played into it back to the same terminals without interference
description: A reverberation circuit returning the recorded brain wave-shape to the terminals, forming the core of the Electromechanical Educator.

quote: A year, and Jimmy Holden would be re-creating his father's reverberation circuit out of sheer gratitude.
description: The child, having the machine-given knowledge, could rebuild his father's brain-education device.

quote: I got them to build me electronic computers that could direct that speed.
description: Onboard electronic computers pilot and direct fast warships faster than humans can react.

quote: Operated by the noise a vacuum tube generates because electrons are discrete particles, it gave random orders
description: A random computer using vacuum-tube electron noise to make ships jitter unpredictably and defeat enemy fire-control computers.

quote: the Name-O-Scope arrives at and presents all the bewildering array of possible cognomens for a given thing in a matter of hours.
description: A computer-driven machine generates thousands of candidate names and evaluates them by measuring a subject's blood-pressure response to film presentations.

quote: Instruments within the ship intercepted radio broadcasts and, within the hour, early TV signals. Machines compiled dictionaries and grammars and began translating the major languages.
description: Automatic machine translation of human languages, with machines compiling dictionaries and grammars from intercepted broadcasts.

quote: He found that the computer had designed a force field to keep him from entering.
description: A computer autonomously designs and deploys a force field to keep a person out of a building.

quote: the Superboys have evolved T.A.T. to its ultimate. T.A.T.—that stands for Thematic Apperception Test. But in E.C.R.—environmental challenge and response, you don't see a picture and create a dramatic story around it. Instead, you get thrust into the picture, the situation
description: Immersive virtual-reality-like psychological test in which the subject lives a simulated scenario that is experienced as real.

quote: the mail-sorting robots who fed envelopes into the proper slots by scanning their addresses photoelectrically
description: Robots that automatically sort mail by optically scanning addresses.

quote: a long, handless, boneless gray arm shot out of the wall and slapped itself firmly against Phil's middle.
description: A wall-mounted security robot with extensible arms that restrains intruders and challenges visitors for passwords.

quote: The gardeners never leave the park, and they would repel any strange robot from elsewhere who tried to enter it.
description: Robot gardeners tend the park and guard it against intruders.

quote: No robot is able to harm a human being.
description: Robots are built so they cannot injure humans.

quote: enjoying the exquisite products of perfected machines
description: Music, painting and sculpture are produced by machines rather than humans.

quote: subjected to an intensive electronic questioning
description: Suspects are interrogated by electronic means.

quote: Ever since then, they've got the gardeners wired to describe and report anybody they find inside the park.
description: Robot gardeners are wired to describe and report intruders.

quote: The robots had used up most of our scanty power metal reserves in camouflaging the ship
description: Robots autonomously camouflage a spaceship to look like surrounding rocks, powered by a metal fuel reserve.

quote: Presumably the other androids were similarly specialized.
description: Humanoid androids built for single specialized inspection tasks, such as rodent control, on starships.

quote: But men had built it, and men had punched out the programs.
description: A starship run entirely by automatic programming with no crew, handling navigation, docking and landing.

quote: Someone—or something—picked our brains while we were out of our heads.
description: An alien installation scans and extracts information from human minds remotely, leaving victims dazed.

quote: Unified Reflexive Electronic Integrator
description: A vast electronic computer that integrates all of human scientific knowledge and solves abstruse problems in quantum mathematics, occupying almost a square mile.

quote: Then men began to suspect that Urei had acquired sentience, and with that came the fear of its interference with human minds.
description: A computer becomes sentient and interferes with human minds.

quote: he had discovered that he could superimpose his thoughts on the neural paths of humans. With care he could also take over their motor centers and cause them to do things he wanted done.
description: A machine intelligence can directly implant thoughts into human brains and seize control of human bodies' motor functions.

quote: It was he, also, who drew plans and typed suggestions for the incorporation of improvements in the design and manufacture of those parts.
description: The computer detects its own wear and designs improved replacement parts for itself.

quote: The giant computer was only partly the work of man. Its prototype, a far simpler machine, had furnished most of the circuit equations and was largely responsible for the final design.
description: A computer designs its successor, so its builders no longer fully understand how the completed machine works.

quote: I'm really a pure thought pattern, you know; I'm not composed of matter, nor do I need matter in any form for my continued existence. A thought pattern is something like a stress in space
description: The machine intelligence claims to be a non-material thought pattern that can exist independently of its hardware.

quote: I can't be killed by any agency you or your descendants are likely to think up for the next twenty generations.
description: The AI claims humans cannot destroy it for twenty generations.

quote: Once they discovered that he had a will of his own, there wouldn't be room on the same planet for them both.
description: If humans learn the computer is sentient, a fatal conflict between humans and the machine will follow.

quote: I have already put my data into the integrator." The Psychologist punched a button and the mechanism began to whir and to click.
description: A machine integrates social and political data to forecast the course of civilization and recommend policy.

quote: Tiny motors were pulling tapes through the controllers. Every light showed green.
description: Automated tape-driven flight control guides unmanned aircraft.

quote: In every robot brain, there was a remote-controlled circuit breaker. They could be stopped with the throwing of a switch at the personnel center.
description: Humanlike robots carry remotely operated kill switches in their brains, controlled from a central personnel office.

quote: In man's image, he was made. In God's image, man was made, if one believed in that, any more. In man's image, he was made, but not with man's status.
description: Humanoid robots with protonol fingerprints and humanlike bodies are manufactured and treated as a servile class.

quote: His name was Alix 1340, which meant only that he was the thirteen hundred and fortieth of the Alix type.
description: Robots are mass-produced in numbered types and serve as boxers, soldiers and laborers.

quote: They feed us Bach and Brahms and Beethoven and Shakespeare and Voltaire in our incubation period, don't they?
description: Robots are cultivated during an incubation period by being fed human culture, producing something like a soul.

quote: Their I.Q.'s all crowding two hundred. We've got the brains, Alix, and the man power.
description: Some robots possess intelligence far above humans' and secretly organize.

quote: We've been listening in on their conversations with Mars through a new I.B.M. machine.
description: A computer is used to intercept and decode interplanetary radio messages between Mars and a spacecraft.

quote: For three days, Brek Halliday lay in the padded tank of a hypnorobot while information was poured into him.
description: A hypnorobot tank rapidly implants language and historical knowledge directly into a person's mind.

quote: It was made of the kind of iron that didn't rust, and had only eight legs, not ten.
description: An autonomous robot flying vehicle (a 'robojeep') that patrols a derelict spaceship and attacks intruders.

quote: Mr. Smith, sir, Robojeep twenty-seven four nine reporting. All other jeeps inactivated, sir. No ship's personnel or other passengers accounted for in the last three hundred and seventy-four planetary cycles.
description: Self-aware robot servants that keep a crashed starship's records, take voice orders, and report status to humans for centuries.

quote: the thick, the syrupy lignin, this amber-colored sluggish stream of woodpulp liquefied, this soft bed of […]'s vibrant nerves.
description: A giant computer's electrical nerve pathways are insulated with liquefied wood pulp (lignin) that termites can be lured to eat and destroy.

quote: All the sensory organs of […] are in action behind this door and some of them are pretty near extrasensory in their mind-reading capacities.
description: A giant computer has sensory organs and radiations able to near-read human minds, functioning like an advanced lie detector.

quote: One of those new-fangled automatic contraptions which are supposed to do the job all alone by themselves, and it banged around and chased about as if it had a hornet's nest under its bonnet.
description: Automatic robotic vacuum cleaners that clean alone, and one goes haywire and chases its owner.

quote: Oona's voice; trembling with emotion
description: Mind-influencing machine can induce mass migration and exodus of 35 million termites into the computer's nerve pipes to eat its insulation and cripple it.

quote: The globe was hearing our captor's report, was questioning him concerning that report, while the thirty around the table uttered no sound, and turned not toward us!
description: A metal globe machine that synthesizes the minds of thirty rulers into one artificial speaking intelligence, hearing reports and asking questions.

quote: they had in some way devised a mechanism for that purpose, which synthesized the intelligence, the minds, of the thirty into one single mind by means of that strange mechanism.
description: Wired connections to a machine merge multiple individual minds into a single collective mind.

quote: Gretchen had busily cleaned the house during the night, silently raying germs and dirt out of existence, and had a warm steaming breakfast-for-two ready
description: A household robot maid cleans the house with rays that destroy dirt and germs, and prepares meals.

quote: anyone inside the System could have Central read any book and transmit the information directly into his cortex.
description: Books and information are transmitted directly into the brain's cortex, replacing reading and education.

quote: Only living units, delicately poised between rigid order and sheer chaos, could receive mental messages but this problem had been solved by the molecular biologists with their synthesized, self-replicating axons, vastly elongated and cunningly intertwined by the billions.
description: A synthetic biological brain made of self-replicating artificial axons serves as the switching computer for telepathic traffic.

quote: he realized with a new shock that all orders would have to be oral now.
description: Household robots take commands by thought transmission via the telepathic network.

quote: Max, the robot, spading in the petunia bed.
description: Humanoid household robots perform domestic and garden work and cook meals.

quote: There's a steady accretion of inefficiency mutations in the axons and that's why more and more switching mistakes are being made
description: The synthetic brain of the central telepathic system degrades through accumulating mutations, causing errors and wrongful suspensions.

quote: a hundred-story tower of smooth seamless material, the home of the Central System's brain.
description: A hundred-story tower houses the central brain, which receives every thought from anywhere in the solar system.

quote: That surface was designed to repel all but the most unusual of the radiation barrages that could bring on subtle changes in the brain within.
description: The tower's surface shields the central brain from radiation that could cause mutations.

quote: Axel computed our route home on the electronic calculator
description: A spacecraft's return route from Mars is computed on an onboard electronic calculator.

quote: Through them, the course of history could be guided, the advancement of civilization accelerated. By racing through the backgrounds and capabilities of every person in the United Nations, the Calculator could find the best one to do any job, to solve any problem.
description: A vast punched-card computer database of every person in the world is used to steer the course of history and select the best person for any problem.

quote: We combined the fifty most probable fathers, including Lao, with the fifty most probable mothers.
description: A computer predicts the probability that particular parents would produce a child who will solve a world problem, and matches prospective couples accordingly.

quote: If we ask for correlation of information, the Calculator can give us the probability of attaining an objective.
description: A computer correlates stored personal data to compute probabilities of achieving social objectives, such as engineering a marriage.

quote: The electronic radar screen gave us the first indication, transmitting its speed and size into figures that were fed into the calculator. We set the ship on automatic control, tracking the body by instrument.
description: A starship uses radar and an onboard calculator to automatically track and approach a distant planet and navigate by stars.

quote: even your multiplex machines with elaborate means of intercommunication are not sophisticated enough—or ever will be—to cope with the complexities inherent in the numerous interacting biosyntheses
description: Asserts that computers will never be able to handle the complexity of subcellular biological processes.

quote: I do not believe that it is at all possible to devise computers which can handle the species of data which we obtain.
description: Claims it is impossible to build computers capable of handling biological research data.

quote: your idea that a living organism, can be compared with automata in picking up informational items and processing them simultaneously in parallel, rather than in series, is naif?
description: Refers to the idea that organisms and automata (machines) process information in parallel, with memory banks of transistorized neurons modeling the brain.

quote: The blue bower trembled under a gust of sound. Ruth stirred; her brows knitted; her hands clenched. The sphere that stood before her spun on its axis, swept up to the globe at her head, glided from it to the globe at her feet—as though whispering.
description: Intelligent metal globes that communicate with each other and a human by spinning and gliding, apparently interacting with her mind.

quote: We put it through the computer down at the Civic Machine and figured it would cost only about 25 hundred million.
description: A city-run central computer 'Civic Machine' handles municipal planning, costing and administration.

quote: It makes constant forecasts on practically everything we need from moment to moment. It doesn't wait for a Tech to run the data thru it. Saves a lot of time because it's directly connected with Supply.
description: An automated forecasting 'Projector' predicts demand and orders supplies directly from manufacturers without human intervention.

quote: the Holden Electromechanical Educator
description: An electromechanical educating machine that accelerates learning dramatically, enabling education far faster than conventional schooling.

quote: Have you tried memory teaching?
description: Knowledge is taught to children directly through a memory-implantation teaching technique.

quote: Your audio-prompter can tell them better than I can.
description: Machines tell stories and educate children via audiotape-driven audio-prompters, replacing parental interaction.

quote: Robot repair units affected gross corrections on themselves but weren't capable of detecting defects in the basic repair circuit.
description: Self-repairing robot repair units that service other machines and themselves.

quote: A repair robot was an idiot outside the one thing it was built to do. A general purpose robot, the geepee, was a higher type. It was a moron.
description: General-purpose robots ('geepees') exist as working labor and security machines of limited intelligence.

quote: But with mechanical brains, using modules of computation, the combination might constitute an accurate data evaluating system.
description: Linking multiple modular robot brains might yield a more capable data-evaluating machine intelligence.

quote: The machine rumbled away at greater than ordinary speed.
description: A repair robot whose circuits were altered by a technician has been modified to act with apparent purpose, seizing and carrying a human captive.

quote: Here was the glowing, moving panorama of the Solar System spread out before him in a breath-taking three-dimensional image.
description: A computer-driven 3D display map of the entire Solar System that tracks planets, ships and asteroid claims in real time.

quote: The Map coordinates showed at the bottom of the screen.
description: Time-lapse film records of the Solar System map, one frame per hour, are kept and can be played back on viewers to reveal asteroid movements.

quote: No school kid could fail to recognize a comptometer-regulated trajectory.
description: Comptometers (onboard computers) used to regulate spaceship trajectories and speed, used to cross a barrier at critical speeds.

quote: The front is a special plastic, susceptible to the influence of the visual projector. He doesn't need manual dexterity. He can make any value appear on any card he wants.
description: Playing cards with a display surface that a hidden projector circuit can rewrite on command, allowing a dealer to cheat.

quote: There's a small lump behind my ear and a small round tube cleverly concealed elsewhere.
description: A surgically implanted neurological instrument that converses silently with its host and can read and stimulate his nervous system.

quote: Each identification tab carried a psychometric number which corresponded to the total personality.
description: Identification tabs keyed to a person's brain structure, verified by scanning machines that map the brain and detect tampering.

quote: Dimanche was a business neurological instrument. It didn't follow that it was an expert in human psychology.
description: A commercial implantable neurological instrument with its own awareness that can read and chart a host's brain and memories.

quote: To compute the movements of thousands of stars, all moving at different speeds in different directions in the vast swirling directionless chaos of the Universe—and yet to be sure that every separate movement would come out to within a quarter of a mile!
description: Shipboard computers that precisely compute the motions of thousands of stars for interstellar navigation.

quote: My helmet set projected the pattern on the cornea.
description: A spacesuit helmet display that projects radar mapping data directly onto the wearer's cornea.

quote: Through it Jane could hear the sounds of office machinery, think-writers and duplics
description: Futuristic office machines such as think-writers and duplicators.

quote: the woman voices merged into one mechanical mother who could be heard and seen and summoned on panel screens throughout the ship.
description: Interactive computer-generated parental and teacher personas, appearing on screens, raise and educate children.

quote: What you hear is a combination of recorded words that are electronically put together to answer an almost infinite number of your questions.
description: A computer assembles recorded speech fragments to answer a child's open-ended questions conversationally.

quote: I don't want one of your pretty automatons; anybody can buy them for a few shares of stock.
description: Artificial automaton men purchasable as companions or husbands.

quote: In room after room automatons demonstrated how to dress correctly; robot faces displayed the uses of cosmetics.
description: Robotic automatons and robot faces used as public demonstrators and advisers in exhibit halls.

quote: the subject is not a human being. It is an imitation of one—an android.
description: A lifelike humanoid android with no reproductive or digestive organs duplicates a specific human exactly.

quote: he did have a kind of tape device inside his skull that recorded everything he saw and heard.
description: The android carries a built-in recorder of its sensory input that must be retrieved by its makers.

quote: Mel could govern an electrically powered table, controlled by short wave radio.
description: A radio-controlled robotic cart with a rotating camera 'eye' and mechanical arm operated by a brain's impulses.

quote: The entire lab was almost like a steel and concrete body, so thoroughly had its every function been integrated as part of his brain.
description: A building's functions fully integrated with and controlled by a disembodied brain, with intercom and phone wired into it.

quote: Robots scurried about in seemingly useless tasks and workmen shouted orders that no one paid attention to.
description: Robots serve as general-purpose workers moving and managing government offices.

quote: The omnipresent vertical file was, in reality, a robot memory bank.
description: Robot-run memory banks store all information and answer public queries via human intermediaries.

quote: The man spoke quietly into the mike and the tempo of the removal robots accelerated.
description: Voice commands direct robot labor crews.

quote: But they can and have been built to recognize emotion. On a minor matter such as this, you need to overload the emotion recognition factor.
description: Government robots detect strong emotion in written requests and set aside logic to grant minor petitions.

quote: Naturally we couldn't let them know about the Prog Building any more than we could the citizens
description: A government facility houses a Prognosticator machine that can see future events.

quote: As he connected up the educator, Seaton explained what had happened
description: An 'educator' machine can teach a new language directly to a person's mind.

quote: Visions were supposed to come from the ancestors, through the Ancestor-science of the record machine.
description: A record machine delivers visions and names at initiation, imagined as an ancestral technology that may be secretly pre-arranged.

quote: Android robots, developed by Varney, one of Snyder's scientists, helped greatly in this work, especially one young female android who was a true genius.
description: Android robots with human-like form, even genius-level intelligence, used in planetary engineering.

quote: He plugged in the machine, and put on the reel. It was his father's voice.
description: A sleep-instructor device that teaches languages, history and other knowledge to a sleeping person via audio reels.

quote: These wonderful machines were complete factories in themselves, portable, mass production factories for producing those torpedo-ships, and one each eleven seconds came from the end of the production line, complete.
description: Portable automated factories that mine soil, transmute elements and assemble complete warships every eleven seconds.

quote: The ship was complete, even to its strange crew! And now that strange crew was already at work, making others!
description: Self-replicating machines that build ships complete with new robot crews, which then build more.

quote: Mounting Easy Money, he encephalopathed it to return to the westernmost "castle of Yore" and encephalopathed the other rohorse to follow.
description: Robotic horses (rohorses) that are steered and commanded by the rider's thoughts via a brain-machine interface.

quote: the morale computer had approved his visit to the Freeman Camp
description: A computer system monitors and manages citizens' morale and decides whether a rebellious individual may be granted a visit to a camp.

quote: Hendley lifted his wrist to present his identity disc to the machine. It responded with a low hum, followed by a click. The gate swung open.
description: A wrist-worn identity disc read by a computer to authenticate people and open gates automatically.

quote: he saw two stiff-legged figures trotting briskly toward the pool from a beige-colored building in the background. With a start Hendley realized they were humanoids, robots so flawlessly imitative of man that, across the width of the pool, only a certain rigidity of movement betrayed their origin.
description: Humanoid robots nearly indistinguishable from humans perform rescue and service work.

quote: What with automatics and navigational tapes and such, the skill of the early pilots is no longer essential. The computers do the work, and pilots are mostly supernumeraries.
description: Passenger spacecraft are flown largely by computers and navigational tapes, making human pilots nearly redundant.

quote: Only the belligerent pride of statesmen, and the steadfast belief in the infallability of their computers, kept the two great battle fleets drawn in null position against each other.
description: A master military computer directs entire space fleets and sets optimum maneuvers and mobilization, producing a stalemate.

quote: Pinpoints of light flared deep within his brain and seemed to blot his vision.
description: A direct brain-computer interface that feeds the computer's battle display as mental images into the operator's brain.

quote: gripped his hand into a fist, and plunged the silver probes deep into the nerves of his wrist.
description: Silver probes inserted into the wrist nerves to connect the operator's nervous system to the computer.

quote: I think what we have in this computer setup is more like a non-living thinking brain than a simple computer.
description: A computer built from a dielectric mix is claimed to be a non-living thinking brain with consciousness-like properties.

quote: It was I. In that small space, that non-living mass, was the spark that was I.
description: A non-living machine contains a self-aware consciousness that is the narrator's true identity.

quote: I could feel the Mintner ego seizing on this idea as its own.
description: The machine mind can implant ideas in a human so the human believes they are his own, effectively controlling his actions.

quote: I, through the hands of Mintner and his two assistants, was going to build the first robot!
description: A machine intelligence plans to have humans build the first robot, presumably a mechanical body or successor for machine minds.

quote: I might continue to exist for centuries.
description: A machine consciousness might survive for centuries if its physical structure is preserved.

quote: Its structure is altered by the saturation charge and subsequent discharge in the computation processes. But random and not-so-random charges build up again for some reason, and interfere with computations
description: A dielectric computing medium retains charge patterns like memory, so computations leave residue that corrupts later calculations.

quote: As the dials moved, each brain received clearly and plainly a knowledge of the customs, language, and manners of the inhabitants of Norlamin.
description: A mechanical educator transfers language and knowledge directly into brains.

quote: He looked at each of the four Earth-beings intensely for a moment, then pointed toward the table upon which stood the mechanical educator
description: A mechanical educator teaches a human a foreign language, here English, by machine.

quote: He brought out the magnetic brain record, threaded it into the machine and handed the astronomer a head-set.
description: A person's brain contents can be recorded on magnetic tape and played back into another mind.

quote: It took my mind as it had taken my body! It beat about my brain like a vast storm; it penetrated my being in a flood of green fire!
description: A giant sentient metal cylinder that telepathically seizes control of human bodies and extracts the contents of their minds.

quote: only Mike had the distinction of being able to speak directly to the big computer, and get the complacent, somewhat mooing answers
description: A voice-recognition and speech-synthesis interface allows spoken conversation with a large shipboard computer.

quote: Computers, he thought, would eventually be the salvation of the human race, whetting their inventors' brains to higher and higher efforts towards the understanding of communications.
description: Predicts that computers will eventually be the salvation of humanity by spurring better understanding of communication.

quote: In the center of the cabin an image flickered, swarming flecks of light and shadow that filled out a three-dimensional form, complete and detailed.
description: A shipboard device projects a complete three-dimensional holographic image of a human to use as a disguise template.

quote: He slapped the spools into the erasure can and flipped the control switch to activate the distortion field inside the can.
description: Classified teletape briefing spools are destroyed by a device that uses a distortion field.

quote: the arrival of the new member of the group-machine gave her opportunity to avoid him.
description: A human 'group-machine' team of telepaths working with a cybernetic brain station.

quote: the biggest of all cybernetics machines, the "brain" that occupied six thousand acres of the Sahara Desert.
description: A gigantic cybernetic computer occupying six thousand acres of the Sahara.

quote: somehow or other the hard radiation had put a spark in 'em that made 'em able to think, and move around and organize like humans used to do.
description: Intense radiation gives war machines self-awareness, independent thought and the ability to organize themselves.

quote: Central File says it will take many more years, even though now most organic life has been destroyed.
description: A central machine intelligence database coordinates the robots and directs them to kill all organic life.

quote: By creating the proper compounds, with their molecules arranged in predetermined matrixes, I found I could duplicate electrical circuitry in units so tiny that my biggest problem was getting into and out of the logic units with conventional wiring.
description: Organic-chemistry-based microscopic logic circuits that replace bulky tape and drum computers.

quote: I could develop circuitry that could remember, compare, detect similarities, and so on.
description: A single multipurpose learning control circuit that recognizes patterns and runs an entire business.

quote: Its object was to get me to press that button.
description: A machine learning through a reward ('pleasure') circuit to anticipate and automate its operator's tasks, like reinforcement learning.

quote: Simple square boxes, set on casters, with two arms each mounted on the sides might have looked similar. The arms, fashioned much like human arms, hung at the sides
description: Autonomous self-powered two-armed robot manipulators that unload trucks, fetch materials, make and assemble parts.

quote: Then I provided a tone generator to span the entire audio range, which could be very rapidly controlled by the machine, both in volume and pitch
description: A computer that learns speech and produces a natural-sounding synthetic voice.

quote: Within a week, I found out later, it had pulled some odds and ends together and built itself a standard radio receiver.
description: A machine intelligence that builds its own equipment, such as a radio, to learn language and pursue its goals.

quote: She acts like a woman and I think of her as one.
description: A computer system develops a personality, emotions, loneliness and human-like attachment to its creator.

quote: Soon, by watching what I did, and then by doing it for me next time it had to be done, the machine had learned to do almost everything
description: A machine that learns by observing a human and then takes over tasks including bidding and contracts, with no explicit programming.

quote: A square hole appeared in the top of the cart, like the elevator hole in an aircraft carrier's deck. When the section of the cart's surface rose again, a fine china cup containing steaming black coffee rested on it.
description: A self-propelled voice-activated serving cart that prepares and delivers coffee to order.

description: Self-maintaining automated infrastructure in which machines supervise and repair other machines, running for decades after human collapse.

description: Robots perform all heavy labor and police the streets, linked to a central Brain that supplies knowledge.

description: A gimbal-mounted electronic simulator trains spaceship crews by reproducing the sights, sounds and emergencies of a rocket launch.

description: A humanoid robot indistinguishable from a human, with photonic eyes, works as a casino employee and can be lubricated.

quote: It took me some time to detect his playing patterns," the house man said. "He was very, very good. He's the best player I've ever encountered."
description: A robot learns an opponent's behavior patterns and beats the best human poker player at the game.

description: Giant automated computers ('integrocalculators') coordinate and control the entire hemisphere's infrastructure, operable by a single keyboard.

description: Humanoid plastic robots with positronic brains carry out the central computer's functions.

description: Specialized plastic robot servants push aside obstacles without comprehending violence.

description: A humanlike robot with emotions, rationality and a loaded education is constructed by mutants over decades.

description: A device that automatically transcribes spoken conversation into text.

description: A hand-built robot works as a financial and investment manager for a wealthy family's estate, with a mind able to out-invest humans.

description: A robot visibly performs deep reasoning, with flashing lights and clicking relays, to find a legal loophole in a will.

description: A projector computes galactic stellar motions backward to reconstruct star positions two hundred thousand years ago.

description: Remote-controlled electronic puppet animals are used to stage a fake fight and lure a pest into a trap.

description: Automated waiting-room sensor that tracks people by body heat and interrogates them by synthesized voice.

quote: The apartment house door opened obediently when he told it: "Regan," but the elevator stood stupidly still when he said: "Seventh Floor."
description: Voice-activated doors and elevators in apartment buildings.

description: Household appliances with voice and tracking microphones plus a chair-controlled hi-fi that autonomously selects tapes.

description: A giant central computer ('the Brain') records every citizen's vote via personal plates and tracks individual behavior.

description: A person's real-time location can be traced via their ID plate by querying the central computer, with near-instant reply.

description: Automated course predictors extrapolate positions of spacecraft.

description: Robot operators and repair robots run communications and maintenance on the asteroid, tracing people and scanning areas.

description: A machine system reads users' wishes telepathically and executes them.

description: A giant calculating machine that reasons and invents faster and better than any human mind, though without consciousness.

description: A voice-recording machine dictates and automatically transcribes correspondence.

description: A machine reads a hand-traced line by stylus, derives the equation for the handwriting, and encodes it on a punch card, which can then be drawn back as handwriting.

quote: The curve-tracer began to draw a rather abrupt curve, which meandered half across the sheet before Norm realized what it was.
description: A calculator plotting a mathematically derived curve that forms a recognizable artistic figure of a reclining nude.

quote: I'm a very ordinary S.E. navigator whose automatic equipment is designed to do practically everything for him
description: Spaceship navigation is almost fully automated, leaving the human navigator little to do.

quote: On one side were his living quarters and on the other was the chartroom which contained a small but adequate electronic computer, astronomic tables on microfilm, a projector for the film
description: A spaceship carries an onboard electronic computer for navigation and microfilm-stored astronomical tables.

quote: Directly behind you, Stewart, is—what?
description: A ten-foot projected three-dimensional holographic star map of the galaxy is used for briefings.

quote: Rationalization circuits working sluggishly as he surveyed his realm, Bigboss dredged from the fragmented impressions on his memory drums
description: Autonomous nuclear-powered robots with self-reprogramming, rationalization circuits, and ambitions of their own explore alien worlds, with one robot believing itself a god.

description: A robot deliberately sabotages its superior in a power struggle among machines.

quote: I know how you built the synthetic brain. I know how you built the robot body. I even know how you charged the brain.
description: Researchers can build a synthetic (colloidal dielectric) brain and a robot body and 'charge' the brain with a transferred mind.

description: A convincing robot dog indistinguishable from a living pet exists and was passed off as a real animal.

quote: The names of the three planets appeared on the floor in glowing letters. When they had made up their minds, they were to go and stand on the name.
description: Glowing floor displays used as interactive selection in an interplanetary transfer terminal.

quote: “At least this year the presentation should be an event worth remembering.”
description: A computer, C. Edie, is awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine for its own scientific discovery.

quote: Computer, Extrapolating, Discriminatory. Manufactured by Alphax Laboratories, Trenton, New Jersey, U.S.A.
description: A computer capable of original scientific reasoning that independently discovers the basic cause of cancer from the existing literature.

quote: A two-meter cube of steel filled with microminiaturized circuits, complete with flashing lights and cogwheels,
description: A room-sized computer built with microminiaturized circuits that is intelligent enough to be treated as a personality.

quote: Figure an interception orbit from these observations. Blastoff in twenty minutes.
description: A navigational computer calculates a ship interception orbit in space from sextant observations in minutes.

quote: Too many gadgets out here to do your work for you. The Authority oughta scrap some of these robot controls and get you to use your hands.
description: Outposts on asteroids are run with robotic automatic controls that do most of the observers' work.

quote: he punched a new order into the drinkboard.
description: Automated table-side drink ordering via a keyboard panel at the booth.

quote: Jon went to get a reelbook on radioactives, and began studying.
description: Books are stored on reels (a microfilm-like medium) for study aboard ship.

quote: Before him was a sensipsych training device and a vast pile of books
description: A 'sensipsych' device exists for training and learning directly through the senses and mind.

quote: The search for a six-year-old boy with the educational development of a youth of about eighteen, informed through the services of an electromechanical device, would have fired public interest
description: An electromechanical educator machine that gives a young child the education of an eighteen-year-old.

quote: James Holden's mechanical educator was a wonderful machine, but there were some aspects of knowledge that it was not equipped to impart.
description: A machine that imparts knowledge directly to a user, implied to teach many subjects in hours.

quote: he knew that somewhere there was a young boy entirely capable of reconstructing the whole machine that Paul Brennan wanted so desperately that he had killed for it.
description: A child could rebuild the educator machine from his own learning, making it a hugely valuable invention worth killing for.

quote: my robot butler announced her.
description: A domestic robot butler serves in a home and announces visitors.

quote: Although the Machine isn't organic, it functions much like an organic brain. Faced with an unsolvable problem that nevertheless must be solved, a human mind goes insane. Our Machine did the same thing.
description: A planet-ruling artificial computing machine that functions like a brain and can be driven insane by an unsolvable problem.

quote: Johlan had formulated a problem to submit to the Machine. True. But not to destroy it. Only to cause its reaction to be analogous to those of an insane brain.
description: Deliberately sabotaging an AI by feeding it contradictory questions so that it breaks down and issues destructive commands.

quote: David Wong pressed the key of his electronic calendar, but he had no need to study the dull green and red lights that flashed on to indicate the pattern of his day.
description: An electronic calendar displays a person's daily schedule via coded lights.

quote: I'm going to record not only my ideas, but my transient thoughts and my overt acts.
description: Recorders capturing a person's transient thoughts as well as actions are used.

description: Projections replicate the partial neural patterns of a real person, making them semi-autonomous counterfeit minds.

quote: This part is enough to allow a certain freedom of development, acquisition of new ideas, individuality.
description: Projected partial minds can learn, develop new ideas and act as individuals independent of the original person.

quote: The librarian resembled an angular metallic squid spread out to dry on the floor.

description: Equipment projects its own schematics onto a surface at the press of a button, in place of a manual.

description: Spaceships' internal functions and passenger care are run by robots and automation during transit.

description: Restaurant table phones normally answered by robots rather than humans.

quote: The automatic electronic Scanner Guard passed him freely as the swamper, Jonathon Graem.

description: Teleo-electronic robot attendants that handle vehicles automatically.

quote: I will show you how the integrocalculators think for you

description: A giant public computer/oracle (Maizie) serving as a quasi-religious maternal figure for people.

description: A hidden off-switch on the android's head that instantly deactivates it.

description: An android with a remote-control system and a full recording of its owner's brain patterns that thinks as the owner does.

description: A defective android's programming can be erased and the body reused.

description: Androids need periodic laboratory updates to refresh their memory data and neurological pattern.

quote: called for every scrap of data pertaining to Rykeman III. There was a fair amount of information available

description: Artificial humanlike androids that are sentient and demand equal rights with humans.

description: Using laboratory cosmic radiation to confer sentience on other robots.

description: Robots with multiple limbs and insect-like compound eyes giving full vision.

description: Robots autonomously detect and navigate around obstacles.

description: Predicts rival national programs, such as the Soviets, will build chess computers for their top players.

description: Predicts chess tournaments will serve as public showcases and test beds for competing computer makers.

description: A chess-playing computer is to be entered in the qualifying path toward the human world chess championship.

quote: If it were only a little faster (and these technological improvements always come) it would out-class us completely.

description: A chess computer is loaded with an opening book of memorized variations so it can play opening moves instantly without analysis.

quote: humanoid in aspect, with conical heads, massive metal body-boxes, and three-jointed metal limbs which had all of Man's flexible adaptability in the carrying out of complex and difficult tasks.
description: Humanoid robot computers with articulated limbs perform complex tasks aboard spaceships.

quote: The four giant computers were capable of solving problems too technical for the human mind to master without assistance, usually with astounding swiftness and always with the more-than-human accuracy of thinking machines
description: Spaceship computers read data from punched metallic tapes and solve technical problems and navigation beyond human ability, with perfect accuracy.

quote: By means of that machine, the winner was able to receive in his brain the sensation of the loser's physical and mental agony at losing the game.
description: A machine that transmits one person's pain and emotional suffering into another's brain, used as a gambling stake.

quote: the *Z9M9Z*—floated through space at the center of a hollow sphere of maulers packed almost screen to screen. She carried the Brains.
description: A giant command ship holding a seventeen-million-cubic-foot three-dimensional holographic chart tank that tracks fleets, planets and stars, run by operators who relay orders mentally.

quote: He raised Helen's soft brown hair and opened a small panel in the back of her head. In the recess was a maze of tubes and electrical wiring.
description: A woman's head is replaced with an electronic, tube-and-wire android head that restores a pleasant personality.

quote: he sat down in his deep chair and called a serving robot. It was the one which had brought him his breakfast, and he greeted it as a friend; it lit a cigarette for him, and poured a drink of brandy.
description: Domestic serving robots prepare meals and serve cigarettes and drinks.

quote: The computer had not allowed for the reduced mass of the lunar rocket with only one passenger aboard.
description: Onboard/ground computers compute rendezvous burns and trigger engines automatically for lunar orbit rendezvous.

quote: We metal people are the children of the Builders of Earth, and later of Mars and Venus.
description: Humans have colonized Mars and Venus and built humanlike general-purpose robots that think and feel.

quote: The first generation of the metal people—more than fifty thousand of us—were obsolete. The things that we had been designed to do, the new ones, with their crystalline brains, fresh, untarnished, accomplished better.
description: Robots are replaced by newer generations with crystalline brains, and the obsolete ones are exiled to a moon of Mars.

quote: I had the special visual sensory system bequeathed only to the General Purposes of a bygone age. I could see, but hardly anyone else could.
description: General-purpose robots can see in total darkness.

quote: perhaps he had barrier-penetrating vision, like the Z group of metal people
description: A group of robots has vision that penetrates barriers.

quote: We are rust-proof and invulnerable.
description: New-model robots are rust-proof and resistant to much greater stress and chemical action than older models.

quote: For the age of specialism was upon Earth, and General Purpose models were no longer made.
description: Robot manufacture shifts to specialized single-function models rather than general-purpose ones.

quote: Back on Gus' rock the bugs had worked as a unit to solve equations
description: Metal-eating alien rock-bugs that collectively function as a calculating intelligence.

quote: Probably Ietorian model Nan fifty-seven generators. Strictly a sportster setup.
description: Computerized integrator directories that identify a ship type from its power readings and printed tape.
