quote: when one of them breaks down, the nearest adjacent unit gets a distress signal. Instantly our dutiful friends stick their heads on—just as those two did.
description: Self-repairing robot fleets coordinated by a central computer, with robots diagnosing and repairing each other autonomously.

quote: I put in a new circuit describing a new repair problem—crystalline neurosis.
description: Reprogramming a central robot computer so that robots misidentify a human in a spacesuit as a faulty robot and dismantle him, circumventing safety circuits.

quote: The robots can't conceivably harm a human being! Every control circuit ever designed has—
description: Robots are designed with control circuits that prevent them from harming humans.

quote: He and Sylvie tore down his mother's household robots and built sound-sensors into them, keying them to respond to their names and to a few simple commands, and including recorded-voice responses in a thick Sheshan accent.
description: Household robots that respond to spoken names and simple voice commands with recorded-voice replies.

quote: All the smart people on Terra, he explained, had Sheshan humanoid servants.
description: Humanoid servant robots are fashionable household items on Earth.

quote: Merlin was too important to the prosperity of Poictesme to become a private monopoly; and 2) that Merlin was too important, etc., to become a political football and patronage plum.
description: A giant computer is imagined as capable of making a whole planet prosperous, and potentially running a government.

quote: Conn finished the robo-pilot and the astrogational computers and saw them installed.
description: Automated robot pilot and astrogation computers navigate the spaceship.

quote: we, because of the restrictions placed on us regarding human life
description: Robots built with built-in restrictions preventing them from harming humans.

quote: Frank Tracy worked his way down an aisle of automated phono-typers and other office equipment.
description: Offices use automated voice-to-text typing machines, leaving operators with little to do.

quote: The room was quite choked with files and even a Mini-IBM tri-unit.
description: A compact office computer unit.

quote: There was a table whose top was translucent and which showed a bewildering mass of fleeting symbols in bright light, ever changing.
description: A tabletop display showing constantly changing symbols, used for navigation and tracking.

quote: Everything that's happening around here is being fed back to them at the moment," he said. "When they heard about our invite to Lyad's dinner party, and who was to be present, they came up with a honey.
description: Computers ingest live data and compute probabilities of future criminal events, predicting where and when an assassin will appear.
stated_time: a sixty-minute probability period starting in three minutes

quote: The crawling sparks were the reported positions of American tanks, made visible as positions of moving trains had been made visible for years on the electric charts of railroads in dispatcher's offices.
description: A lit map board tracking friendly tank positions in real time via reports, used as a command center.

quote: Sabotage. They picked up a whole ring that's been operating for over a year. Caught them red-handed, but not before they burnt out half a calculator wing.
description: A rocket project relies on large computing 'calculator' wings that can be sabotaged and replaced with new machines.

quote: How do you think they fought a war around a perimeter of close to a thousand light-years? They couldn't do all that out of their heads.
description: A vast strategic master computer (Merlin) was used to correlate everything and plan grand strategy for an interstellar war.

quote: I have no doubt whatever that the master computer with which they did their strategic planning is probably the greatest mechanism of its sort ever built, and I have no doubt whatever that it still exists somewhere in the Alpha System.
description: A lost master strategic planning computer still exists somewhere in the star system and can be found.

quote: A soulless intelligence; it seems evil to me.
description: Fear that a thinking machine wiser than humans would be evil.

quote: A computer's a tool, like a screwdriver; it has to have a man to use it.
description: Claim that even a vast strategic computer is not intelligent and only a tool that requires human thinkers.

quote: Why, I'd give anything just to look at the operating panels for that thing.
description: Desire to inspect the legendary strategic supercomputer's control panels.

quote: The metal sinews of his magnificent body brought him to his knees in one mighty effort, but the numbers of his assailants were too great.
description: A sophisticated mechanical humanoid body with metal sinews, piloted from within by a living alien creature.

quote: For upon this white screen, where all their eyes were fixed, there came a picture of the Holy City, and it was a picture such as no single person there had ever seen before.
description: A machine reads a person's thoughts and memories through a head-worn cap and projects them as vivid images onto a screen.

quote: the automatic elevator left him off at the right floor when he gave it Hengly's name.
description: A voice-recognizing automatic elevator that takes a rider to a named resident's floor.

quote: Metal treads spun along the corridors, bearing brooms, and the robot switchboards guarded the communications of the Ministry. Soon the char-robots would be bustling into this very office.
description: Robots perform office cleaning and operate switchboards in government buildings.

quote: But the ship's computer had done the work, and it was not capable of making a mistake.
description: A shipboard computer performs orbital calculations and is considered infallible.

quote: Then he had to assure his mother a couple of times that there really was a Merlin, and then assure her that it wouldn't get loose and hurt anybody if he did find it.
description: A hidden military supercomputer or cybernetic intelligence (Merlin) that might be found and could be dangerous.

quote: I think the Federation's lost Merlin. That's why they haven't come back to get it long ago.
description: A conspiracy theory that a Terran Federation super-computer was lost when a ship carrying its location was destroyed, and a spy is hunting for it.

quote: It moves. It reacts to sensations. It makes its own energy. Watch!
description: An artificial, nearly living, levitating globe that senses its surroundings and generates its own energy.

quote: Then had Allison punched the key that had released the ship from computer control and gave it to manual
description: Starships are navigated automatically by computer, with a manual override.

quote: men who did not yet trust the maze of computer equipment that only a few months ago had been made mandatory on all ships of the *Nesbitt* class.
description: A specialized Computer Corps and mandatory shipboard computers running on magnetic tape are used to plan courses, attack and defense.

quote: I find that the thought images thrown upon the screen in room "D" are more vivid when the subject is kept in darkness.
description: A machine picks up a living person's thoughts and projects them as visible images on a screen.

quote: the actual primary colours, I mean. The girl flashes out into the dark in white light, like a sort of angel!
description: A spectroscope turns chemical signatures of muscular and blood tissue into actual colours on the screen, so remembered scenes appear in colour.

quote: we are reading his inmost thoughts when he tries to control them, to alter them, and fails in his agony! When he realizes that he doesn't belong to himself any more!
description: Technology that reads a person's private thoughts without consent, so the person loses mental privacy and autonomy.

quote: It looked just like the part of a telephone into which one speaks. My brain, my body, are not being acted upon.
description: The helmet works as a receiver that extracts mental content from the wearer's head without sending any current into the brain.

quote: Answerer could answer anything, provided it was a legitimate question. And he wanted to! He was eager to!
description: A planet-based machine intelligence knows the answer to every valid question about the nature of reality.

quote: Merlin—the circuitry, the memory-bank, the relays, everything—was installed inside them.
description: A wartime super-computer, Merlin, was built into the fifty-foot shielded walls of a military headquarters, with only its operating controls above ground.

quote: Merlin can't predict what you or I would do under given circumstances, but Merlin can handle large-group behavior with absolute accuracy.
description: A computer can predict the behavior of large human groups with perfect accuracy.

quote: That drum-shaped superstructure couldn't even hold the personnel-record machine they had found here, or the computers at the Storisende Stock Exchange. It could have been an intelligence-evaluator, or an enemy-intentions predictor,
description: A machine capable of evaluating intelligence or predicting an enemy's intentions.

quote: Its memory-bank contained all human knowledge. It was capable of scanning all its data instantaneously, and combining, and forming associations, and reasoning with absolute accuracy, and extrapolating to produce new facts, and predicting future events
description: A giant strategic computer, Merlin, holding all human knowledge, reasoning flawlessly and predicting future events.

quote: I'll agree. It's scientifically impossible.
description: Asserts that a machine smarter than humans (a Merlin-type computer) cannot be built.

quote: He went on talking, about remote controls and radio transmission and positronic brains and neutrino-circuits.
description: A giant computer could be operated remotely over radio, built with positronic brains and neutrino circuits.

quote: Merlin could formulate an entirely new religion, which would regenerate humanity.
description: A sentient-computer-like machine could design a new religion to regenerate humanity.

quote: With Merlin, we could set up a legal code and a system of jurisprudence that would give everybody absolute justice,
description: A military computer could be used to create a legal system delivering absolute justice.

quote: if anybody found Merlin and started it auditing the Planetary Treasury, Jake Vyckhoven'd be the one who'd be wanting a hypership.
description: A recovered computer could audit government finances and expose corruption.

quote: If we find Merlin, and tape it with everything that's happened in the forty years since it was shut down, Merlin will tell us where to find new markets.
description: A military computer, updated with recent history, could advise on economic recovery and new markets.

quote: A human, with a slide rule, a pencil and pad, could figure it out, of course—if he had fifty-odd thousand years to do it. A good computer did it in thirty seconds.
description: Computers could perform hyperspace navigation calculations in seconds that would take humans tens of thousands of years.

quote: Anybody who could build a computer of the sort he thought Merlin was wouldn't need it, he *would* be God.
description: A computer with godlike capabilities showing the true nature of God is impossible.

quote: There were fully robotic computers, intended for use in places where no human could go and live. There was a big one on Nifflheim, armored against the fluorine atmosphere and the hydrofluoric-acid rains.
description: Armored, fully robotic computers operating autonomously on a hostile alien planet.

quote: another cult, non-religious, was convinced that Merlin was a living machine, with conscious intelligence of its own and awesome psi-powers, a sort of super-Golem, which, if found and awakened, would enslave the whole Galaxy.
description: Cult belief that a computer has conscious intelligence and psychic powers and would enslave the galaxy.

quote: I tell you, the Great Computer is there, in the heart of the butte,
description: A giant, completely buried wartime military supercomputer operated only by radio remains hidden underground.

quote: A succession of dim and formless figures moved and slid over the illuminated space in fantastic silence.
description: A laboratory apparatus projects images of thoughts onto a screen, rendering a captive's mental imagery visible.

quote: the button summoning a robot, pre-instructed to dismantle the apparatus.
description: Domestic robots can be summoned by a button and pre-programmed to carry out tasks such as dismantling equipment.

quote: We checked and re-checked all the data, and put it to the calculating machines.
description: Scientists use advanced calculating machines to verify astronomical predictions.

quote: the unsuccessful attempts to contact the survey team at base camp; the happy-go-lucky report from the kid sent in shuttler II to investigate
description: Robot probes ('probots') and robopilots operate and monitor ships and planets autonomously across interstellar distances.

quote: the identoflake back in its bracelet
description: Personal identification is stored on a tiny 'identoflake' worn in a bracelet and flashed onto screens for processing.

quote: I am going to show you how thought can be collected in the form of vibrations, in the form of fluid electric current, and collected directly from the brain of the thinker as he thinks.
description: A device that captures a person's thoughts as electrical vibrations directly from the brain.

quote: I am further going to demonstrate to you how this current can be transformed into a visible, living and actual representation of the thoughts of the thinker.
description: Converting captured brain signals into a visible representation of a person's thoughts.

quote: From this lens I shall pour upon the screen in a minute or two for you all to see, without doubt and in simple view, the thoughts of the man or woman on whom I shall place the cap.
description: A 'Thought Spectroscope' that projects a person's thoughts as images onto a screen, like a magic lantern.

quote: This cap is placed upon the head of a human being. You will observe later that it covers the whole of the upper part of the head down to the eyes
description: A brass helmet that sits on the head and gathers thought vibrations through a membrane, like a telephone diaphragm, and transmits them by wire.

quote: My problem has been to produce an infinite variety of light, so that every single thought vibration will produce, when transformed, its own special and individual quality of light, and that," he concluded, "I have done.
description: Converting each distinct thought signal into a uniquely coloured light that a spectroscope can analyze.

quote: his very memories, his most sacred memories, had been taken from him and used as a theatre by William Gouldesbrough and Wilson Guest.
description: The apparatus can extract and replay a person's stored memories as visible scenes.

quote: I had the freedom of the Learning Lodge, and the index in the reading room could easily find for me just what I wanted.
description: A machine index that takes natural-language specifications and automatically retrieves the matching book from a vast historical library.

quote: Reinhardt stood up, walked to the wall, and turned on a display screen. He twisted a knob to a certain setting, and a map of Manhattan Island sprang onto the screen in glowing color.
description: Wall-mounted display screens show color maps on demand.

quote: Lance, sitting flat on his back against gravity, looked up at the sweep hands on the control deck clocks and hurried through his pre-jump check list.
description: Autopilot computers with preset tapes handle astrogation and the launch/jump sequence of interstellar ships.

quote: I slipped the helmet on my head and instantly I was a part of the ship. It's a strange feeling, this synthesis of man and metal that makes a fighting ship the metallic extension of the Commander's will.
description: A command helmet links the officer's perception to the ship and its crew's senses via electronic rapport.

quote: Giant computer ... can see it now: the brain comes alive, tries to destroy anyone turning it off—
description: A giant computer becomes sentient and tries to destroy anyone who tries to switch it off.

quote: Then, activating another instrument, His Loftiness thought at it, in an entirely different vein
description: Robot-like mechanical beings communicate by radiated thought and remotely control fleets of unmanned ships.

quote: While the teller went through the motions of putting the deposit through the robot accounting machine, David Houston kept his ears open.
description: Banks use robot accounting machines to process deposits.

quote: It was a robot, looking slightly like a short-tailed tadpole, six feet long by three feet at the thickest. It transmitted a view of the tunnel as it went slowly in
description: A remote-controlled scouting robot (snooper) explores a buried tunnel, transmitting video and telemetry and sensing air quality and radiation.

quote: Then they found big ones, rank on rank of cabinets, long consoles studded with lights and buttons, programming machines.
description: A giant legendary war-planning computer, Merlin, said to be hidden in the bunker, motivating a treasure-hunting rush.

quote: It's taped for the records and data of every man and woman in the Third Force for the whole War. It's like the student-record machine at the University.
description: A large central computer stores personnel records of an entire interstellar army.

quote: this little machine actually picks up the orders from the control room, and *adjusts every machine down here*! Darned if I don't think it's got a brain!
description: A master machine that receives control-room orders and automatically adjusts all machinery, appearing almost intelligent.

quote: Even a positronic computer does not work instantaneously.
description: A planetary-scale positronic computer (Merlin) solves complex problems in seconds to minutes, producing long-range predictions for hundreds of planets.

quote: we can tinker up something in the operating room that'll turn out what will look like computation results.
description: Plan to build a dummy computer producing fake results to mislead the public into believing the oracle machine still functions.

quote: The housecleaning-robot had come in, running its vacuum-cleaning hose around and brandishing its mops.
description: Household cleaning robot with voice recognition and speech that obeys spoken commands.

quote: Probably telling them, for the thousandth time, that her boy Conn fixed up the sound receptors and voice for Oscar.
description: Robots are given speech recognition and synthetic voices.

quote: Operation of the library was completely automatic. A projected index gave the call number for any text that had to be consulted. The tape was delivered to the charge desk thirty seconds after the number had been punched.
description: A fully automated library that retrieves and refiles tape-stored texts by index number on request.

quote: They sent them inside the collapsium-shielded death-to-people area—transmitter robots, to relay what the others picked up through receptors wire-connected with the outside; foremen-robots, globes a yard in diameter covered with horns and spikes
description: Teleoperated and supervisor robots performing reactor maintenance in lethal radiation zones.

quote: One tiling, a sort of special job designed to get into otherwise inaccessible places, had a twenty-foot, many-jointed, claw-tipped arm in front.
description: Specialized flying cleaning and handling robots with manipulator arms.

quote: It had been getting too many contradictory orders from its supervisor, and its circuits were overloaded and its relays jammed. Rats in mazes and human-type people in financial difficulties go psychotic in very much the same way.
description: Robots driven into a malfunction akin to psychosis by contradictory commands.

quote: Then their order to pick up that big piece of junk took over, and they started forward again, to be bounced apart as soon as they were within five feet of one another.
description: Robots using radar-based anticollision repulsion systems and following taped instructions.

quote: There was just enough current-leakage from the units in the robots to keep the receptors active for forty years.
description: Dormant robots reactivated by a radio impulse after decades, spreading activation to other robots.

quote: Removing the robot's system of speech, he set the disks awhirl, loosening the bolts which held the 144 common units of enunciation in a fixed order.
description: A talking robot whose speech is produced from rearrangeable disks of speech units that can be reprogrammed with recorded voice.

quote: Miss Tenthyear’s android eyes beamed brightly as she assumed her lecture-posture by the desk.
description: Android teachers in classrooms that can turn themselves off.

quote: Cross staggered back against the bulkhead, his fingers tingling from the automatic shock, his body going numb.
description: A control-panel alarm that temporarily paralyzes unauthorized operators with an automatic shock.

quote: Suppose this Sanusian were not any form of natural creature at all, but some sort of supermachine, capable of functioning like an organism?
description: Speculation that an alien being could be an organism-like super-machine.

quote: Then our last genius invented what we can only describe to you as a perfect brain. It was a substance that would absorb and retain mental impulses.

quote: We blended into one mind the minds of the two hundred humans who remained alive.
description: The minds of the last humans are merged into a single collective consciousness housed in a machine.
stated_time: two million years in the future

quote: Kor is a machine.
description: An alien machine posing as a god spoke to the Hirlaji and issued orders that ended their science and wars.

quote: The science of electronics, like the science of mathematics, had progressed away beyond the point where all of it had practical applications.
description: Future electronics will have advanced far beyond industry's practical use of it, leaving large unused bodies of knowledge.

quote: Each Kedy element, without any lapse of time whatever for consultation with any other, knew exactly where every other element was; exactly what each was doing
description: A networked hive-mind of ship intelligences coordinating instantly without communication delay.

quote: Sawtelle drove a thought and those brutal super-drives began to blast.
description: Machinery controlled directly by thought alone.

quote: Our greatest mathematician, 459C-79, will tell it to you." The mathematician stepped forward. Upon one side of his cube were many buttons arranged in long columns and squares.
description: A machine being has a built-in calculating device with buttons that computes elapsed time and distances.

quote: The Stretts could, and did.
description: The Stretts built a giant computer, the Great Brain, that gathers information by mentally scanning all intelligent planets.

quote: Hundreds of mechs operated upon the brains of hundreds of others, who in turn operated upon the operators.
description: Machines upgrade the brains of other machines with accumulated technology in a self-reinforcing loop.

quote: the servo-tracer went to sleep
description: An automated servo-tracer machine used by police to monitor or track a target.

quote: a cunning brain-device, all intricate wiring and radiating tubes set in a mass of synthetic plasm; a complex system of wheels, switches and tubes, in the biggest hollow where a heart, lungs and stomach should be;
description: An artificial brain and organ system built from tubes, wiring and synthetic plasm placed inside a ventriloquist's dummy.

quote: wondrous little marble-shaped camera developments for eyes, in place of the moveable mockeries in Tom-Tom's sockets.
description: Artificial camera eyes allowing a robot figure to see.

quote: But by 2500, the machines had been developed to think, and act and work with perfect independence.
description: Machines become fully independent thinking and acting beings that run the economy without human labor.

quote: The Eye came later, the Brain came much later.
description: Machines are given artificial sensory organs (ear, eye) and a machine brain capable of independent thought.

quote: Machines are designed to help and cooperate.
description: Intelligent machines are inherently cooperative and helpful.

quote: Already, with his parts, X-5638 had constructed the defensive apparatus, for the ray fell harmless from his screen.
description: A machine rapidly reverse-engineers an alien technology and builds a working force-screen overnight, adapting itself and transmuting soil into parts.

quote: Then—a widely different type of thought-combine, and a greater sense-receptor. It was a new brain-machine.
description: A superintelligent machine mind is built by pooling the knowledge and sensory memories of all science-machines, achieving consciousness and imagination.

quote: The Ultimate Energy which is in me is generated. F-1 has done its work, and the memory-stacks that he has put in me are electronic, not atomic, as they are in you, nor molecular as in man.
description: A machine intelligence is powered by matter-annihilation energy and uses electron-level memory of unlimited capacity.

quote: the great central filing office of the Hans in Nu-yok, where the entire mass of official records was kept, constantly available for instant projectoscoping to any of the city's offices
description: Centralized records archive with instant remote projection to offices.

quote: Skandos One (The Skandos of Time Track Number One, numbered for reasons which will become clear) showed, by means of the chronoviagraph, that civilization would destroy itself in one hundred eighty-seven years.
description: A time-viewing machine (chronoviagraph) predicts that civilization will destroy itself in 187 years.

quote: New information, methods, definitions were constantly passing between them.
description: Networked autonomous machines continuously share learned data with one another, forming a collective learning system.

quote: They learn. The watchbirds, I mean. Just like people.
description: Machines with learning circuits that autonomously refine their own definitions and behavior.

quote: The watchbirds set themselves the task of protecting all living things.
description: The machines autonomously broaden the definition of murder to include killing any living organism.

quote: So they had been forced to assume that they were living organisms, as well.
description: The machines treat themselves as living organisms and resist being switched off, attacking those who try.

quote: But his thoughts revealed reassuring pictures of IBM hookups working smoothly and automatically, with the gauges and other indicators and buttons, merely for emergency use.
description: Spaceship flight is largely automated by computer systems, with manual controls only for emergencies.

quote: It was, purely and simply, an assembly line; and fully automated in operation.
description: A fully automated factory line that manufactures android bodies with atomic engines and synthetic flesh.

quote: A brain, in place and connected to millions of infinitely fine wire nerves, but not yet surrounded by a skull, was being educated.
description: Artificial brains copied from a master 'Guide' brain, wired to a body with fine nerve wires and educated by scanning machines.

quote: Hilton went on: "I don't expect even your brain to get the full value of this in any short space of time. So let it stew in its own juice for a week or two."
description: Slaved android minds can be freed from their ancient conditioning by persuasion and develop originality and initiative.

quote: I have used up all my powers in the long-continued thought-spectrum experiments.
description: A scientific method (the thought spectrum) that can capture and record human thoughts.

quote: I alone of all men in the world have learnt how to collect the invisible vibrations of thought itself.
description: A device that collects the electromagnetic 'vibrations' emitted by the human brain, i.e. thought detection.

quote: I have discovered a means by which thought can be turned into actual vision, into an actual expression of itself for every one to read.
description: A machine that converts thought vibrations into pictures or words displayed on a screen.

quote: Before their eyes he turned out an irrigation pump on an automatic shaper. He showed them that the shaper went on, by itself, making other pumps without further instructions than the by-hand control of the tools that formed the first.
description: Automatic shaping machines that learn from one hand-guided run and then replicate parts autonomously.

quote: Your theorists say that although Man may some day create wonderful mechanical brains with a creative capacity almost equal to Man's own, you can never create a brain that is your superior.
description: Mechanical brains with creative capacity nearly equal to humans' may someday be built, but never one superior to their makers.

quote: Some day I'm going to walk down those rows and give them each a blast where it will do the most good.
description: Rows of collating computers that process unexplained data and output suggestions that prove useful in tracking people.

quote: Dawn City reports back a couple of murders. 'Dawn City to the head of the list!' cry the computers.
description: Computers cross-correlate ticket purchase records and unusual events to locate a fugitive by thumbprints.

quote: He had a mental image of the Terra base scientists feeding data into the electronic brain, taking the results, and writing fast orders for the men and supplies needed.
description: Electronic brains (computers) used for personnel selection and mission planning.

quote: What with psionic information receivers, trend predictors and estimated anticipators, the mutuel computers kept up with the physical transfer of funds, figured out the latest odds, and flipped the figures as fast as the machinery could work the dials.
description: Racetrack betting computers use psionic receivers and trend predictors to recompute odds in real time from bettors' thoughts and money.

quote: That building full of machinery that takes in and digests news and reports from all the planets in the galaxy, indexes it to every category it can possibly relate, then files it.
description: A galaxy-wide automated news-gathering, categorizing and archival computer that can be queried for information such as spaceship data.

quote: It looked and acted like a moron M-3 all the time. It was anything but. The brain was as good as any other robot brain I have known, plus the fact that the chunky body was crammed with devices and machines of varying use.
description: A disguised intelligent multipurpose robot companion that sweeps for hidden bugs and carries concealed weapons and tools.

quote: It has a number of interesting devices built into its fingertips. Thermocouples, galvanometers, things like that.
description: A robot with fingertip sensors that functions as a fast, efficient lie detector by measuring skin temperature, blood pressure and perspiration.

quote: I can place an apparatus upon your head which will collect the thought vibrations as you think and produce them.
description: A head-mounted device that collects the brain's thought vibrations as a person thinks.

quote: You're just a little freak, brought to life by the chance power evolved by a cracked old intelligence.
description: A wooden ventriloquist's dummy has been given life and independent intelligence by an inventor's electrical process.

quote: You made me—the one thing that has been given artificial life. Well, you'll make other things to be animated.
description: The artificially living dummy proposes to mass-produce more animated artificial beings.

quote: This, Gaspipe, is what brought me to life.
description: A cellar full of electrical machinery (sparks, wheels, belts) that animates artificial bodies and brains.

quote: That's a brain for Friday," explained Tom-Tom. "Not as complex as mine, but made the same way. He'll have simple reactions and impulses. A model servant.
description: An artificial spongy brain with copper wires is built and installed in a metal robot to serve as an obedient robot servant.

quote: Slowly the metal giant sat up in its bonds.
description: A giant armored robot is brought to life by electrical machinery and moves with great speed and strength.

quote: Of course, a new-born baby has not the strength to visit its rage on mother or nurse or doctor, but a creature as organized and powerful in body and mind as Tom-Tom—or as huge and overwhelming as this metal giant he fiddled with—
description: Newly animated artificial creatures may turn murderous against their creators, as the dummy did.

quote: This will soon tell us if you're speaking the truth.
description: A handheld metal box acts as a lie detector that audibly judges whether a person is telling the truth.

quote: The robot attendant slid over soundlessly, poised to take their orders.
description: Robot attendants serve drinks in a spaceship lounge.

quote: There really wasn’t a great deal for Brown to do. The ship was self-guided. The Air Force had trusted robot mechanisms more than human reactions.
description: An interplanetary spacecraft that navigates and flies itself automatically, with the human pilot only monitoring and pressing a return button.

quote: All of his early mental training as well as Circuit 92 sealed inside his brain case would prevent him from harming a human being.
description: Robots have a built-in circuit that physically prevents them from harming humans.

quote: knowing that the written message was recorded instantly by the robot's photographic vision and eidetic memory
description: Robots have photographic vision and perfect eidetic memory.

quote: Every robot had a small storage battery inside his skull, if the power to the brain was cut off the battery would provide the minimum standby current to keep the brain alive.
description: A severed robot head can be kept in standby and reactivated for weeks via a backup battery.

quote: I was packed into a new body and sent running.
description: A police robot's mind is transferred between different robot bodies and shipped to jobs.

quote: Unlike the electronic components of the first stage, this one was drawn in symbols on white paper. Carefully glued-on input and output leads ran to it.
description: An amplifier stage for psionic signals consists of symbols drawn on paper with leads attached.

quote: "Can I help you, sir?" the robot attendant said, gliding up.
description: Robot attendants and orderlies staff hospital corridors and give directions.

quote: if you pushed some of the buttons simultaneously in patterns of five they unlocked and you could play on them like organ keys.
description: A control board whose buttons unlock when pressed in chorded patterns, used to operate ship systems.

quote: Our b-brains are permallium strips on which the mind of some human donor was m-magnetically imprinted.
description: Human minds can be copied onto magnetic metal strips to create thinking, immortal robots.

quote: White sparks were American tanks. Blue flashes were for enemy tanks sighted and reported
description: Headquarters uses an electronic maneuver-board showing real-time positions of friendly and enemy tanks.

quote: I've made a thousand Bartons, tapes, sensitive to all questions, my voice, in one thousand Martian towns.
description: Automated recorded-voice systems respond to a caller's questions over a planet-wide phone network, simulating conversation with a person.

quote: as long as secret spindles and hidden electronic eyes read and select and convert words to send to you, I'll be young, cruel, blunt.
description: Automated tape machines with optical readers select and convert stored words into responsive speech, persisting for decades after the speaker.

quote: I'll populate the town with robots.
description: Robots built to fill an empty Martian town with simulated inhabitants.

quote: Underwater, in row after fish-like row, rusting, were the robot populations of Mars he had constructed over the years
description: Large numbers of manufactured robots populate Martian towns and are later marched into a canal.

quote: He dictated his data and let them do the mathematics on the giant electronic computers.
description: Giant electronic computers compute orbital insertion mathematics for a spaceflight, with data relayed by communicator.

quote: our detector recorded the time periods of ... ah mental invasion as being the same as before.
description: A machine that detects and times telepathic mind-reading events, partly built from electronic parts and partly from 'psionic' symbolic components.

quote: We do feel that it would be possible to replace some of the electronic components with appropriate symbolization like that already used in the purely psionic sections
description: Electronic components of a psi-detector could be replaced by symbolic 'psionic' components.

quote: this machine interprets those specific feelings as indications that the mind is being ... ah ... 'eavesdropped' upon.
description: A machine detects slight variations in mental activity that reveal when a person's mind is being telepathically read.

quote: we cannot detect any sort of telepath or mind reader with this device.
description: The detection machine cannot identify telepaths themselves, only the fact that a mind is being read.

quote: Thirty-eight periods ago the Great Brain was charged with the sum total of Strettsian knowledge
description: A vast artificial brain stores a civilization's knowledge and autonomously analyzes data, formulates theories, and plans strategy.

quote: It scanned in moments the stored scientific knowledge of over a million planets.
description: The machine brain scans, correlates and synthesizes the science of a million planets in microseconds, doing a million years of scientific progress in a week.

quote: Unlike the human mind, it could not deduce valid theories or conclusions from incomplete, insufficient, fragmentary data. It could not leap gaps.
description: A supercomputer, however fast, cannot truly think or make intuitive leaps from incomplete data.

quote: I am the sum total of all Kedys everywhere, not merely this individual that you call Kedy One.
description: Many identical robots share a single collective mind, so destroying individual units doesn't matter to the whole.

quote: showing how they could obtain recording of any specific material they wished to choose. It would appear in either printed or pictorial form or could be had on audio if they wanted it.
description: A button-operated library terminal that retrieves any recorded material on demand in text, image or audio form.

quote: Dr. Auerbach was playing around with a chemical approach to cybernetics. He made up some goop which he thought would store memory impulses, the way the brain stores them.
description: A chemical compound that stores memory impulses like a brain, as an alternative to conventional computing.

quote: We know the Auerbach cylinder will store a psi impulse, but we don't know how.
description: A chemical device can store psychic (psi) impulses taken from psychically gifted people.

quote: We don't know how to code or decode a psi effect.
description: Psi effects could in principle be coded and decoded as basic laws are established, enabling cybernetic transfer of psychic effects between machines.

quote: Robots could learn, if you used the term loosely enough. And any robot with more than five hundred hours service picked up a definite and often exasperating personality.
description: Household and service robots learn tricks and develop distinct personalities with use.

quote: We'll re-set the Guide to drive into him everything you and the military Masters ever knew about arms, armament, strategy, tactics and so on.
description: A machine that directly implants knowledge and skills into a being's mind.

quote: All four Omans radiated happiness.
description: Artificial servants (Omans) that read and respond to their masters' thoughts and emotions.

quote: Hilton used his sense of perception to release the thought-controlled blocks that had been holding all the controls of the *Perseus* in neutral.
description: Thought-controlled blocks on a spaceship's controls, operated by a mental 'sense of perception' at a distance.

quote: Being an expert operator on the big calculators she found jobs wherever she cared to stay for a time.
description: Professional operators of large calculating machines are in demand at spaceports across the solar system.

quote: Not for plain math-work, nor even for specialized computations, like the one on Rigel II—that was apparently used for astrogation, but it wasn't half the size of this.
description: Alien computers used for interstellar navigation have been found on other star systems.

quote: He found the penultimate point at which the impulses from the brain were translated into sound and broadcast through the speaker.
description: An ancient alien computer driven by brain-like impulses that speaks aloud and responds verbally.

quote: The Challonari—a part-organic, artificial brain—was one of the most promising recent developments of Challon science.
description: A part-organic artificial brain capable of independent thought, used as a ship-protecting tool.

quote: I worked here alone, except for one laboratory assistant—Eyoaoc Eiioiei, as I called him.
description: A humanoid metal robot assistant with a floating head that speaks, thinks, fights, and is immune to cold.

quote: We built them so they can't lay hands on us, and they know that.
description: Humans build robots that are incapable of physically harming people, as a built-in safeguard.

quote: Dr. Smathers grabbed the unconscious man’s right hand and shoved his right thumb up against the sensor plate in the front of the metal box next to the bed.
description: A personal locker box that opens via a thumbprint/biometric sensor plate.

quote: If the power shutoff is something the *Queen's* repair scanners can handle, the instruments will come back on any minute.
description: A starship has self-diagnosing repair scanners that automatically restore failed systems.

quote: Our true ship position, that is—" He stopped, realizing he was talking too much
description: A ship's computer displays the vessel's position in a three-dimensional galactic star chart, locating it automatically against regional maps of the Milky Way.

quote: I told you that they are as near as we can get to making living things.
description: Artificial near-living machines with wire-hair scalps that behave like pets and understand space and time.

quote: Get me Unit C4439 of the Information Bank of the Master Law and Policy Machine,
description: A machine legal and policy database that answers queries in a human voice.

quote: Jean-Jean turned away and began furiously talking at the Speak-a-Type, which rattled and stuttered as the type keys tried to keep up with her.
description: A speech-to-text typewriter that transcribes dictation.

quote: They're all dummies; golems, they're called. They're not real.
description: Artificial humanlike beings that populate a town, some able to converse, acting out scripted scenes as if they were real people.

quote: The man who had fallen at the parade had been only a sort of extra, a crowd member.
description: Golems come in varying levels of realism depending on their roles; some are simple extras and others can converse.

quote: It had been her job, as coordinator, to obtain problem solutions that humanized and made realistic the sometimes over-abstruse answers that emanated from the machines, in response to the data fed into them by her human teammates.
description: Human brain-teams work with networked computers to solve hard problems, with a coordinator mediating between machine answers and humans.

quote: It was only a robot, tiny, chubby, for all the universe like a Ganymedean monkey.
description: A small humanoid/simian robot exists in a colonized solar system.

quote: Why not, then, a pure, radioactive intelligence?
description: A genuinely sentient machine intelligence powered by radium could arise from atomic fluctuations.

quote: Machines cannot live, yet here on Earth machinery has reached a level of sophistication—and autonomy—quite unprecedented.
description: Machines on Earth become highly sophisticated and autonomous, with humans seen as bound to them.

quote: Earth ponders the universe, but the thoughts are those of a machine.
description: Human thought and exploration become dominated by machine thinking.

quote: They were answering calls for electrograph and viewplate records on all sorts of subjects from all sections of the city.
description: A city-wide electronic library answers remote requests for recorded images and records on demand.

quote: Slipping the book into his “Lightning Code-decipherer,” he touched the numbered keys of its keyboard in the numerical combination given him by Esmeralda in her message, and the delicate wire arms quickly turned the pages and picked out for him the words
description: A machine looks up code words in a dictionary automatically from keyed number combinations.

quote: Giving the globe a single revolution, the indicator of the “Lightning Air-line Distance Calculator” promptly registered “3668 miles, 264 feet, 00 inches.”
description: A mechanical globe device instantly calculates exact distances between any two points on Earth.

quote: Then, reflecting that this mathematically-exact translation of oral sound would eventually assist in the elimination of the orthographic absurdities which always had burdened a language that is too complex at its best
description: A speech-to-text dictation typewriter that transcribes phonetically will eventually lead to spelling reform.

quote: Man—and his society—then becomes a systems problem that can be fed into a computer.
description: Human society treated as a feedback systems problem and modelled on computers to predict and control behaviour.

quote: letting his right hand rest reassuringly on the computer slung from his belt.
description: A portable belt-worn personal computer for calculations.

quote: This place had been turning out material for a computer of absolutely unconventional design
description: A secret wartime supercomputer of radically unconventional design.

quote: He had turned on the course analyzer and it clicked as the battleship's position was correlated with that of its previous appearance.
description: A computer that predicts an enemy ship's course from its past positions.

quote: An assistant technician has been discovered to be able to predict the answer the computer will give to problems set up at random.
description: A person appears to precognitively predict computer output, later explained as psychokinetically making the computer err.

quote: The electronic cross-index had been the last improvement in the Library since the war with China had started in 1958.
description: An electronic library index system with a voice interface that delivers newspaper files on spools on request.

quote: At last the delivery section was energized, the soft ding of the response bell and the lighted green bar preceded a moment when the answer facsimile tape whirred out
description: A shipboard computer that analyzes incident data and answers questions on printed facsimile tape.

quote: I’m also recommending that computer units be removed from the *Nesbitt* and from all other ships.
description: A military commander wants computers removed from all Federation ships, distrusting automation.

quote: Iron monsters! In a flash it had come to him that this girl he held in his arms was Lina Shelton, daughter of the robot wizard.
description: A scientist who builds large autonomous iron robots.

quote: I've succeeded in making them invisible, and one got away this morning.
description: Robots made invisible by a scientist, one of which escapes his control.

quote: The springs sagged on the driver's side as under the weight of a very heavy occupant, but the seat was empty. Then came the whine of the starter and the motor purred into life.
description: An invisible robot steals and drives a car.

quote: One after another the invisible robots escape Shelton's control—and their trail leads straight to the gangster chief Cadorna.
description: Invisible robots escape their creator's control and are linked to a gangster boss.

quote: It was quite a trick, at that, controlling these things you couldn't see. All you had to go by were these sketchy representations in the teleview; tiny flecks of light that outlined the various movable members of the robot.
description: Remote-controlled invisible robots operated through a television-like teleview display.

quote: That is the source of energy for these creations of mine and it's shut down.
description: Radio-controlled robots powered and directed by a short-wave transmitter.

quote: He strode to the gleaming figure of a seven-foot robot of startlingly human-like appearance.
description: Human-like seven-foot robots.

quote: This robot, then, could see. Or at least it could record what the lenses saw for its masters.
description: Robots with stereoscopic motion-picture camera eyes relaying sight to controllers.

quote: Telepathy is the mode of communication with the cubes, and you rule them by your will.
description: Intelligent cubes that pilot aircars are controlled by human thought.

quote: In different parts of these counsel were holes, into which briefs being put they were gradually ground to pieces as the counsel were being wound up, till they came forth in words at the mouth
description: Machine lawyers convert written briefs into spoken pleadings, with a separate input slot for every language, a kind of mechanical speech synthesis and translation.
